newsitem.title: SWEDEN: Poll shows fewer see Sweden in EMU in 1999.
newsitem.headline: Poll shows fewer see Sweden in EMU in 1999.

text.p: Three percent of market players believe Sweden will join Europe's economic and monetary union (EMU) from its 1999 start, down from seven percent in March, a poll by TEMO and brokerage Ohman showed on Thursday.
In November 1996, 15 percent of market players expected that Sweden would join EMU in 1999, Ohman and pollster TEMO said in a statement.
The survey also showed that in May, 82 percent believed EMU would start on time, up from 68 percent in March and 80 percent in February. No poll was made in April.
If both Sweden and Germany were members of EMU, market players expected the five-year bond spread to be 37 basis points, down from 45 basis points in March and from 39 in February.
